narrative:
The model estimates a 79% chance that you will leave your current role, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your profile that historically align with employees who eventually depart.

Three factors stood out most in the decision. First, having received other job offers while at the company strongly pushed the prediction toward leaving. Employees who get external opportunities are far more likely to move on than those who do not. Second, your overall career experience of 6–10 years also increased the likelihood of departure. While many who stay have only 1–5 years of total experience, your mid-level tenure matches profiles that tend to explore new opportunities. Third, your relatively short time in this specific organization (1–5 years) further tilted the prediction toward leaving, as longer tenure in one place is more common among those who remain.

These elements together created a clear signal that you may be weighing options elsewhere. The company should discuss your career goals openly with you and explore whether additional responsibilities, growth paths, or retention measures could change your outlook. You, in turn, may want to reflect on what would make staying fulfilling before making any decisions.
